title: Edge gateway request cork and transparent early-abort fix for customer-visible timeouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Production incidents were reported by three customers where client requests to the Hosted API experienced long tail timeouts (up to 30s) followed by 5xx surfaces. Root reproduction shows the edge gateway would 'cork' (stop forwarding) a subset of streamed requests when an upstream worker's KV cache compaction and connection pool resizes coincided with a burst of tenant traffic. Corked requests remained queued behind head-of-line connections; clients retried aggressively which amplified load and caused tenant-level saturation and cascading 5xx. This ticket tracks the urgent bugfix (transparent early-abort + cork release path), QA verification, telemetry rollout, and customer comms.
acceptance_criteria: Edge gateway no longer holds request sockets for >250ms when upstream indicates overload; instead returns an explicit early-abort response with Retry-After header for overload cases
Synthetic replay of previous customer workload (scaled x3) does not produce 5xx waves in staging with the fix enabled
Canary rollout shows <1% error delta and latency tail improvement before graduating to 100%
Dashboard adds per-tenant cork-count and early-abort-rate charts with alerts set to 0.5% of tenant qps
Customer-facing postmortem draft ready and sent to affected customers within 48 hours of stabilization
steps_taken: 03/10: Triage — correlation between KV cache compaction events (runtime telemetry) and increased connection hold times in edge (tracing traces/async spans)
03/11: Reproduced in staging with stressgen scenario derived from customer traffic (pattern: 75% streaming, 25% short requests; burst multiplier 2.5x)
03/11: Captured heap profiles + tcpdump from edge nodes during trial; identified guard path that fails to release cork when upstream returns BACKPRESSURE_OK during compaction window
03/12: Implemented transparent early-abort prototype (edge returns 429 + Retry-After/Retryable header) behind feature flag edge.transparent_early_abort
03/12: Implemented cork-release RPC to upstream runtime to signal immediate KV-compact-scope flush; added idempotent handshake to avoid double-release
03/13: Unit + integration tests added; performance benchmark showing median latency unchanged, 95/99th latency reduced by ~25% under load
03/14: Created canary PR and deployed to two edge shards (~5% of traffic) with oncall monitoring active (links below)
03/14: Drafted initial customer communication template and shared with support and CSMs for review
technical_root_cause: When upstream performed KV cache compaction during heavy tenant burst, the edge gateway entered a cork state for affected request streams but the release path relied on a lease-expiry timer. Under compaction-induced backpressure the lease expiry was delayed and head-of-line request sockets were kept open, causing client retries and amplification. The system lacked an explicit early-abort signal to inform clients to back off gracefully.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs behind feature flag. 2) Canary to 2 edge shards (5% traffic) for 1 hour with active oncall. 3) Increase to 20% for 3 hours if metrics stable. 4) 100% rollout and remove flag after 24h stable. 5) If any tier shows >1% error regression or 95th latency increase >10% in canary window, rollback to previous flag state and run deeper trace capture.
monitoring_playbook: Add alert: edge.transparent_early_abort_rate > 0.5% of tenant_qps (warn) and >2% (critical)
Add alert: edge.cork_hold_time_p50/p95/p99 — critical if p99 > 500ms
On alert: triage oncall, run 'edge dump-cork-states' playbook, capture trace IDs and forward to runtime team
If customer-facing errors observed: activate targeted tenant quarantine and increase per-tenant queue cap temporarily to avoid collateral 5xx
Verify Retry-After headers present in responses and SDKs surface Retry-After semantics in client telemetry
communication_notes: Initial customer message (to affected customers) acknowledges elevated timeouts and explains immediate mitigation: feature-flagged early-abort rolled to canary to reduce client tail-latency and avoid cascading retries
Provide recommended SDK guidance: respect Retry-After, linear backoff, and avoid aggressive immediate retries for streaming endpoints
Offer remediation assistance: rooftop CSM/SE session to replay tenant traffic in staging and recommend batch-sizing/kv-compact windows if needed
follow_up_actions: Postmortem to be authored and published to Confluence (owner: Asha Patel) within 7 days
Design a long-term fix: add leaseless corking path and predictive compaction windowing to avoid compaction during known tenant bursts
Add end-to-end test harness that replays real customer traces (sanitized) nightly to detect corking regressions
SDK changes: ensure Retry-After parsed and surfaced to application code (work item in PM backlog)
Consider dedicated tenant isolation policy for high-burst customers (policy draft in product-management)
